cohort: The study included 100 singleton term pregnancies with cervical maturity induction and anxiety, divided into a control group (80 mL fluid in both balloons) and an observation group (80 mL in vaginal and 100 mL in cervical balloons).
finding: Higher cervical balloon fluid volume was associated with significantly improved cervical maturity, reduced maternal anxiety, shorter labor, higher natural delivery rates, and a lower incidence of complications.
mod_finding: The observation group, receiving higher cervical balloon fluid volume, showed higher rates of natural delivery and lower rates of cesarean section compared to the control group.
